concept: Centralized exchange zero-fee futures programs with API

claims.text: Across MEXC, Phemex and BingX, zero-fee futures headlines come with API carve-outs. MEXC's Jun 1, 2026 notice sets an API schedule of 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker, and says API trading is subject to a separate fee structure that takes precedence over promotional offers such as 0-fee events. The Phemex carnival terms exclude API trading, and BingX's TradFi promotion excludes API trading. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

MEXC's API futures fee notices say API trades follow a separate fee structure that takes precedence over web and app rates and over promotional offers such as 0-fee events and MX discounts. MEXC's own example: BTCUSDT futures cost maker 0% and taker 0.01% on the web or app, but trades executed via API are charged the API rate. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-05-28)

Gate's USDT-M TradFi Perpetuals have a dedicated fee structure effective September 1, 2026. VIP 0 pays 0.0200% maker and 0.0500% taker, and the maker fee is 0.0000% only at VIP 14, VIP 15 and VIP 16, with taker 0.0180%, 0.0150% and 0.0120%. Market-maker tiers pay 0.000% (MM 0) and -0.003%, -0.004% and -0.005% (MM 1 to MM 3). Gate's USDT-M Perpetual Futures Taker Program commences on September 1, 2026, with discounts of 9%, 16% and 20% for monthly taker volume shares of 0.02% ≤ X < 0.2%, 0.2% ≤ X < 1% and X ≥ 1%; participants contact their Account Manager to register. Gate's fee page says users whose API trading volume accounts for at least 60%, or who have reached VIP tier 15 or 16, will be automatically upgraded to advanced institutional users. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-26)

MEXC opened futures trading to the API on Mar 31, 2026, 06:00 (UTC) for users who completed KYC verification, on all futures pairs except Innovation Zone pairs, at 0.01% maker and 0.05% taker. It then raised the API schedule twice: to 0.04% maker and 0.06% taker effective May 1, 2026, at 08:00 (UTC) (notice listed Apr 30, 2026), and to 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker effective Jun 1, 2026, at 08:00 (UTC) (notice listed May 28, 2026). The notices say API trading follows a separate fee structure that takes precedence over web and app rates and promotions such as 0-fee events and MX discounts. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

AlphaX's zero-fee page navigation lists USDT-settled perpetual contracts, event contracts, demo trading, a trading bot and copy trading, with no API documentation link in the navigation read. The KYCnot directory lists the service as Community, Not tested ("We only checked that it meets our listing rules. Its details and score are as the user declared them."), notes "This service is archived. Its site may be gone or now belong to someone else.", and flags Shotgun KYC ("May request KYC or block funds mid-flow, typically via AML checks, transaction limits, or liquidity partner rules."). Confirm API availability and counterparty standing before relying on AlphaX for automated trading. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Binance's fee page lists a regular user at 0.0200%/0.0500% on USDT-margined contracts, with the USDC/USD1 column showing 0.0000%/0.0400% alongside 0.0200%/0.0500%. The 0.0000% USDT maker rate appears only at VIP 9 (at least 25,000,000,000 USD of trade volume and 5,500 BNB), where the USDT taker rate is 0.0170%. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Binance's USDS-M Futures Taker Program applies taker fee discounts on top of the BNB fee discount and VIP tier rates. Users who reach a total Binance Futures trading volume of 100,000,000 USDT equivalent in the last 30 days may apply and are assessed in the Program's weekly review. A limited-time promotion effective from 2026-11-10 06:00 (UTC) until 2027-01-03 23:59 (UTC) increases the taker fee discounts for Tier 2 and Tier 3 from 14% to 15% and from 18% to 20%. Users are removed from the Taker Program if they do not meet the minimum criteria for three consecutive weeks, and can reapply after 3 months upon removal. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10)

On Bybit's help-center fee page, the table for Perpetual & Expiry Contracts Trading (Crypto and TradFi Perpetuals) shows VIP 0 at 0.0550% taker and 0.0200% maker, and Supreme VIP at 0.0300% taker and 0.0000% maker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)

KCEX's own blog says its official fee explanation lists 0% maker and 0.01% taker futures commissions for standard web/app trading, with pair-specific promotional exceptions, and that KCEX does not currently offer API trading access, so this schedule is not an API rate. The source is a KCEX-owned blog that also ranks competitors, so treat comparative statements as promotional. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)

On MEXC's web and app 0-fee futures program, eligibility is granted automatically after regular system evaluations, and certain pairs have a maximum trading volume that is eligible for 0 fees. Events end on short notice: the 0-Fee Fest for LTCUSDT, LTCUSD, FILUSDT, ETHFIUSDT and CRCLUSDT concludes on Nov 23, 2026, 10:00 (UTC). A separate limited-time promotion gives 0% maker and taker fees on DOGEUSDT, DOGEUSDC, DOGEUSD1, XRPUSDT, XRPUSDC and XRPUSD1 from Nov 20, 2026, 16:00 (UTC) to Dec 21, 2026, 15:59 (UTC) for users in selected regions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-20)

Binance's USDⓈ-M Futures Taker Program gives extra taker fee discounts on top of the BNB fee discount and VIP tier rates to users who reach a total Binance Futures trading volume of 100,000,000 USDT equivalent in the last 30 days, apply, and pass the weekly review. From 2026-11-10 06:00 (UTC) until 2027-01-03 23:59 (UTC), the Tier 2 and Tier 3 taker fee discounts are increased from 14% to 15% and from 18% to 20%, and Tier 1 remains unchanged at 10%. The taker discount also applies to TradFi Perps. Users are removed from the program if they do not meet the minimum criteria for three consecutive weeks. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10)

On Bybit's help-center fee page, the Perpetual & Expiry Contracts Trading table shows VIP 0 at 0.0550% taker and 0.0200% maker, and Supreme VIP at 0.0300% taker and 0.0000% maker. Bybit's futures fee page says the MNT discount is not available to Pro-tier users or for API orders, liquidation orders, Trading Bot orders, or Copy Trading followers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-20)

Bybit says its Pro Levels are designed for highly active and professional traders who often utilize API trading. On Bybit's Pro page, Pro 1 requires ≥ 100M 30-day trading volume with API Trading Volume > 20%, and its G1 (Major Coins), Altcoin and TradFi columns show Pro 1 taker 0.028% and maker 0.000% for Altcoin and taker 0.016% and maker 0.000% for TradFi, with Altcoin and TradFi maker 0.000% at Pro 1 to Pro 6. G1 maker is 0.010% at Pro 1 and 0.000% at Pro 5 (≥ 3,000M) and Pro 6. Bybit's derivatives fee update has a complete rate card from Sep 1, 2026. Retail VIP 4, VIP 5 and Supreme VIP derivatives volume thresholds carry the condition API Trading Volume ≤ 20%. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-20)

Bybit's Market Maker Incentive Program help article (last updated on 2026-10-21 07:15:04) lists rebates for Perpetual & Expiry Market Makers: MM 1 to MM 3 earn -0.0010%, -0.0025% and -0.0040% on Group 1, -0.0020%, -0.0040% and -0.0060% on Altcoin, and -0.0010%, -0.0025% and -0.0050% on TradFi, with taker fees based on Pro tier. Levels use a weighted maker share of at least 0.03%, 0.50% and 1.00% for MM1 to MM3, with a weighting factor of 20x for TradFi and 8x for Altcoin. The order size placed by the Market Maker should be at least 10x the minimum order size of the respective Derivatives contracts, applicants contact Bybit's institutional services, and Market Makers' qualifications are evaluated monthly. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21)

Phemex's fee tables show a standing API-share route to a 0.0000% maker rate on contracts. Pro 1 to Pro 4 require API Trading Volume > 20%. Pro 1 (≥ 8M) pays 0.0000% maker and 0.0475% taker; Pro 2 (≥ 100M) pays 0.0450% taker; Pro 3 (≥ 380M and 70% maker) pays 0.0350%; Pro 4 (≥ 1,500M and 70% maker) pays 0.0325%. Phemex notes that API transactions exclude transactions through Broker. VIP1 and above carry an API ≤ 20% condition, and the Standard tier pays 0.0100% maker and 0.0600% taker. Market-maker tiers SILVER and GOLD list rebates of -0.0025% and -0.0050%. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bitfinex's Zero Fees Q&A dated 17 December, 2025 says zero trading fees are applied as the standard pricing for eligible spot, margin, derivatives, securities and OTC trading, with no additional requirements linked to trading volume, holdings of UNUS SED LEO or account tier, and no fixed end date. Margin lending and funding fees are not changing. Bitfinex's live fee schedule lists derivatives trades with maker fees Zero and taker fees Zero. Bitfinex Derivatives lists over 60 perpetual contracts with up to 100x leverage, but its page says the content is intended for an investment professional, a high net worth individual or company, or a sophisticated investor. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

KCEX publishes 0% maker and 0.01% taker for standard web and app futures trading, with pair-specific promotional exceptions, and states that it does not currently offer API trading access. The source is KCEX's own blog, which also ranks competitors, so treat its comparisons as promotional. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Coinperps' base-tier perpetual fee table lists 0.02% maker for Binance, Gate, OKX, Kraken and BingX with 0.05% taker, for Bybit with 0.055% taker, and for Bitget and KuCoin with 0.06% taker. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Zero-fee futures reach API traders through different routes. Retail promotions exclude API traders: MEXC's 0-Fee Fest notice says 'Zero fees do not apply to API trading', and BingX's TradFi promotion excludes API trading. Standing API-share tiers or market-maker programs give zero or negative maker fees: Phemex's Pro1 tier requires API > 20% and pays 0.0000% maker, Bybit's Pro tiers require API Trading Volume > 20% and show 0.000% maker for Altcoin and TradFi, and Binance's Liquidity Provider Program market makers keep their weekly maker rebate tiers for TradFi Perps. Silence about API in a promotion notice is not proof that API orders get the rate. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Do not price an API strategy from a banner or fee-page rate. MEXC's own example says BTCUSDT futures cost maker 0% and taker 0.01% on the web or app, while its June 1 notice lists 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker for API trading. BingX's pilot rules say accounts that have created an API Key are not eligible for the zero-fee policy, regardless of whether API trading is used. Bybit's fee page says the MNT discount is not available for API orders. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

KCEX's blog gives a cost example for a strategy trading $10 million in monthly futures notional through an API, with 60% maker and 40% taker executions. At 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker it computes $6 million × 0.0006 = $3,600 plus $4 million × 0.0008 = $3,200, totaling $6,800. If a trader mistakenly modeled both sides at 0.01%, expected commission would be only $1,000, understating cost by $5,800. The blog calls this an arithmetic illustration of the cited API rates, not an invoice for a particular account, and MEXC's June 1 notice publishes the 0.06% maker and 0.08% taker rates. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)

Bitfinex's notice of Wednesday, June 10, 2026 adds the HYPF0:USTF0, FETF0:USTF0 and XPLF0:USTF0 perpetual contracts, which can be traded with a maximum leverage of 100x, and says traders can access these contracts at zero cost following the implementation of Bitfinex's zero-fee trading policy. The footnote says the derivatives platform is provided by iFinex Financial Technologies Limited. Traders Union reports that Bitfinex has introduced a permanent removal of trading fees for all customers across spot, margin, derivatives, securities, and OTC trading. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Zero trading fees on Bitfinex do not remove every cost. The Q&A says margin lending and funding fees are not changing, withdrawal fees and deposit fees remain in place, the trading fee discount benefit linked to holding UNUS SED LEO no longer applies, affiliates will no longer earn rebates from trading fees, and there is no pool from which to pay developer rebates. The fee schedule charges 15% (of the fees generated by active Bitfinex Borrow loans) and 18.0% when opened by a hidden offer on fees collected by Borrow Funding Providers, and Forbes says the exchange takes 17% to 20% of lending returns from a margin lending market. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Coinperps says that in the 24 hours to 22 November 2026, Bitfinex traded $138.05M in perpetual futures and holds $721.38M in open interest. That is 0.1% of the volume and 0.8% of the open interest across the 22 venues Coinperps tracks, ranking #18 by volume and #15 by open interest, and BTC/USDT is its busiest market at $105.62M. Coinperps also says Bitfinex lists over 60 perpetual contracts. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

MEXC's 0-Fee Fest terms state: 'Institutional accounts, market makers, project teams, and API users are not eligible for 0 fees.' MEXC's own API comparison article says MEXC API spot strategies should budget at the standard 0% maker and 0.05% taker because the zero-fee spot campaign excludes API users, and that the futures API schedule overrides the promotional web rates even when the same account trades both. The headline zero-fee MEXC futures rate therefore does not describe an API strategy. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Binance's notice titled (2026-11-04) says the TradFi Perps taker fee discount reduction announced on 2026-10-28 for VIP 4 to 9 users, from 50% to 40% with effect from 2026-11-05 08:00 (UTC), will not be implemented, and the 50% discount continues until further notice. The promotion announced on 2026-03-31 continues on its original terms, with a Promotion Period of 2026-03-31 02:00 (UTC) until further notice. Regular to VIP 3 users get a 20% discount on taker fees for TradFi Perps and VIP 4 to 9 users get 50%. Its table lists 0.0000% maker, with taker fees of 0.0400% for Regular User and VIP 1, 0.0320% for VIP 2, 0.0256% for VIP 3, 0.0150% for VIP 4 and 0.0085% for VIP 9. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Copies of the superseded Binance 2026-10-28 notice are still online with the old terms. The support-centre page titled (2026-11-05) says it has been superseded by the announcement published on 2026-11-04, but it still lists a 40% discount on taker fees for VIP 4 to 9 users and a VIP 4 taker fee of 0.0180%. A Binance News summary headed 'Binance Futures Will Set Maker Fees to Zero for TradFi Perps' says the update begins 2026-11-05 08:00 (UTC) with a 40% discount for VIP 4 through VIP 9 users. The 2026-11-04 notice says that change will not be implemented and lists VIP 4 at 0.0150%. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Binance's live USDⓈ-M fee page lists a regular user at 0.0200%/0.0500% on USDT-margined contracts; 0.0000% maker on USDT contracts appears only at VIP 9 (at least 25,000,000,000 USD of trade volume and 5,500 BNB, taker 0.0170%). The page says all regular and VIP 1 to 9 users will be able to enjoy 0 maker fee and up to 50% discounts on taker fees when trading any U (United Stable)- Margined Perps during the Promotion Period, and its USDC/USD1 columns show 0.0000%/0.0400% alongside 0.0200%/0.0500% for a regular user. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Binance's USDⓈ-M Futures Taker Program gives approved takers discounts on USDT-M and USDC-M perpetual and delivery contracts, applied on top of the BNB fee discount and VIP tier rates, and the taker discount also applies to TradFi Perps. Users who reach a total Binance Futures trading volume of 100,000,000 USDT equivalent in the last 30 days may apply and are assessed in the weekly review; program qualification criteria use weekly USDⓈ-M Futures Taker Volume Share. A promotion effective from 2026-11-10 06:00 (UTC) until 2027-01-03 23:59 (UTC) increases the taker fee discounts for Tier 2 and Tier 3 from 14% to 15% and from 18% to 20%, and Tier 1 remains unchanged at 10%. Users are removed if they do not meet the minimum criteria for three consecutive weeks, and can reapply after 3 months upon removal. Self trades will be excluded from volume calculations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-10)

Bybit's route to zero or negative maker fees on perpetuals for market-maker flow is an application-based Market Maker Incentive Program, not a retail promotion. New applicants contact Bybit's institutional services with the subject line "Market Maker Application"; all applications and upgrades are reviewed on request and levels are not automatically upgraded; qualification is evaluated monthly; Main Account and Subaccount trading volumes are aggregated; new joiners receive a 1-month trial period; and the order size should be at least 10x the minimum order size. Maker rebates are -0.0010%, -0.0025% and -0.0040% (MM 1 to MM 3) on Group 1 and -0.0020%, -0.0040% and -0.0060% on Altcoin, with taker fees based on Pro tier. Tiers need a weighted maker share of at least 0.03%, 0.50% and 1.00%, with weighting factors of 1x for Group 1, 8x for Altcoin, 1x for Innovation Zone and Pre-Listing, and 20x for TradFi. A Bybit announcement says its program updates the existing API maker rebate schedule across MM tiers. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-21)

On Bybit's help-center fee page (last updated on 2026-11-20 04:29:35), the Perpetual & Expiry Contracts Trading table shows VIP 0 at 0.0550% taker and 0.0200% maker, and Supreme VIP at 0.0300% taker and 0.0000% maker. Bybit's fee page says Supreme VIP is available by invitation for select high-volume traders. The VIP criteria table attaches (API Trading Volume ≤ 20%) to the volume thresholds for VIP 4, VIP 5 and Supreme VIP, and the Supreme VIP row shows N/A in the first two criteria columns, so an API-heavy account may be unable to reach the zero-maker Supreme VIP tier by volume. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-20)

Crypto.com Exchange has run time-boxed zero-fee perpetual programs. A TradFi perpetuals promotion, now labelled ENDED, had a Campaign Period of May 13, 2026 00:00 UTC - June 13, 2026 23:59 UTC with 0% maker fees: Levels 1 - 5 pay 0.00% maker and 0.02% taker, and VIPs 1 - 7 pay 0.00% maker and 0.015% taker, for eligible Crypto.com Exchange users that have access to trade TradFi Perpetual Contracts. A Crypto Perps launch offers zero trading fees for 30 days, with a Promotion Period of Oct 27 – Nov 26, 2026 and a 100% waiver on Maker fees, Taker fees, DCM pass-through fees, and liquidation fees, on BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, ZEC with up to 5x leverage. Foris DAX Inc. is a registered introducing broker introducing customers to Foris DAX FCM, LLC, a CFTC-registered Futures Commission Merchant. The TradFi campaign rules say Crypto.com Exchange reserves the right to cancel, suspend, or postpone the Campaign or amend the Campaign rules without notice. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

Phemex's TradFi futures zero-fee offers were time-boxed and carved out API flow. The announcement sets a Zero Fee Period of February 05, 2026, 11:00 – May 05, 2026, 11:00 (UTC) with maker fee 0% and taker fee 0%, and the note 'Only limited No-API trading vloume' (sic). The Zero Fee Carnival from February 6 to February 20, 2026 lists 'Market maker accounts, API trading, and sub-accounts are excluded' and says standard crypto futures fees (0.01% maker, 0.06% taker) remain unchanged. Whether the three-month window excluded API orders as clearly as the carnival did is ambiguous. (medium confidence)

MEXC API operations carry constraints beyond fees. MEXC's own comparison (data verified as of August 3, 2026) lists weight pools of 300 weight per 10s per IP and 500 per 10s per account, no sandbox for API (web-based futures demo trading only) and 2 fields: API key header plus HMAC SHA256 signature; the launch notice says higher rate limits and dedicated resource support come through an institutional account application; and a Nov 12, 2026 notice says MEXC will gradually migrate its Futures WebSocket market data feeds from JSON to Protocol Buffers (Protobuf). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

MEXC's web/app zero-fee futures program grants 0-fee eligibility automatically after regular system evaluations, based on factors such as account status, trading activity, effective trading volume, risk review and market conditions. Certain pairs have a maximum trading volume that is eligible for 0 fees. MEXC's own pages quote different pair counts: an article verified August 19, 2026 says 320+ perpetuals at 0% on both sides, while the 0 Fee Fest FAQ text says 100+ Futures pairs. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-19)

MEXC's official Futures API provides REST API and WebSocket streaming services. Order placement is POST /api/v1/private/order/create with the required permission Order Placing. Order type 2 is Post Only (maker only), alongside limit, IOC, FOK and market types, and stpMode sets the self-trade prevention mode. Accounts that have not completed KYC can still create an API key but may not be able to enable or use futures order placement–related permissions. API Keys that are not bound to IP addresses are valid for 90 days. Signing uses the HMAC-SHA256 algorithm with a Request-Time header, and a request is invalid if req_time is more than 10 seconds (default) behind or ahead of the server time. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bybit's Aug 10, 2026 announcement says its discount covers 170+ TradFi Perpetual Contract symbols, with availability until further notice, for all TradFi Perpetual Contract symbols (excluding Pre-IPO symbols). The discounted maker rate is 0% against a standard ~0.0200%, and the discounted taker rate is ~0.0275% (varies by VIP level) against ~0.0550%. Bybit's futures fee page has a column labelled TradFi Perps 50% off: a Regular User shows maker 0% and taker 0.0275%, and Supreme VIP also shows a 0% maker rate. TokenPost reports that ANTAUSDT, GLXYUSDT and TMOUSDT were scheduled to start trading on Tuesday, Nov. 17, with a launch promotion that sets fees at zero on limit orders and cuts market-order fees by 50%. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bitfinex's POST /v2/auth/r/summary documentation lists a FEE_INFO array ("Array with info on your current fee rates") whose maker part includes DERIV_REBATE ("Shows the maker rebate for derivative trades on the account") and whose taker part includes DERIV_TAKER_FEE ("Shows the taker fee rate for derivative trades on the account"), plus a TRADING_VOL_AND_FEE array ("Array with data on your trading volume and fees paid"). The documented rate limit is 90 req/min, and the page shows "Updatedover 1 year ago". The Bitfinex Q&A also tells users to review trade history to confirm that fees are set to zero. (medium confidence)

MEXC's 0-Fee Fest FAQ says eligibility is based on factors such as account status, trading activity, effective trading volume, risk review, and market conditions, and is granted automatically after regular system evaluations. Each pair's 0-fee allocation comes with a validity period, and unused trading volume quota is forfeited when it expires. The system may adjust the 0-fee maximum trading volume periodically, including increasing, reducing, or removing the quota. Once the quota is fully used, trades on that pair revert to the standard fee rate. If an account triggers risk control during the event, the 0-fee benefit is suspended until the restriction is lifted, and zero fees do not apply to liquidation. An unofficial SDK README says the set of 0-fee pairs is curated per account and changes over time. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bybit's fee schedule page has a column labelled TradFi Perps 50% off, which shows zero maker rates for the Regular User and Supreme VIP rows. An aggregator article from OneBullEx says that during the promotion period limit orders on the stock perpetual contracts will incur zero fees, while market orders will receive a 50% discount on the standard taker fee. The only API-specific line on the schedule is that the MNT fee discount is not available to Pro-tier users or for API orders, liquidation orders, Trading Bot orders, or Copy Trading followers. The help-center fee page lists Perpetual & Expiry Contracts (Crypto and TradFi Perpetuals) with VIP 0 at 0.0550% taker and 0.0200% maker, so the two Bybit pages differ. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bitfinex API limits are modest for high-frequency work. The requirements page says the current REST rate limit is between 10 and 90 requests per minute depending on the specific REST API endpoint, and that a rate-limited IP is blocked for 60 seconds. For WebSocket, you cannot open more than 5 (authenticated) connections per 15 seconds, and you can subscribe to up to 25 channels at the same time per connection. The REST Submit Order page lists a rate limit of 90 reqs/min. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-17)

MEXC's own comparison article gives a cost example: a spot strategy turning over $500,000 a month with an 80% maker share costs $600 in total fees a year on MEXC's standard spot schedule, versus $240 in maker fees plus $80 in taker fees a month, or $3,840 a year, if routed through the MEXC futures API at the June 2026 schedule. The example is a vendor illustration. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-03)

Binance's 2026-11-04 notice says the TradFi Perps promotion announced on 2026-03-31 continues on its original terms, with a Promotion Period of 2026-03-31 02:00 (UTC) until further notice. Regular to VIP 3 users continue to receive a 20% discount on taker fees and VIP 4 to 9 users a 50% discount, compared to the standard USDT taker fee rate. Its table lists 0.0000% maker for Regular User and VIP 1 to VIP 9; taker is 0.0400% (0.0360% with the 10% BNB discount) for Regular User and VIP 1, and 0.0085% (0.0077%) for VIP 9. On 2026-10-28 Binance announced the VIP 4 to 9 discount would be reduced from 50% to 40% with effect from 2026-11-05 08:00 (UTC); the 2026-11-04 notice says that change will not be implemented. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Binance's 2026-07-02 notice introduces a fee discount promotion for U (United Stables)-margined perpetual contracts, starting with BTCU and ETHU. All regular to VIP 9 users enjoy 0 maker fees during the Promotion Period, which runs from 2026-07-02 10:00 (UTC) until further notice. Regular to VIP 3 users receive a 20% discount on taker fees and VIP 4 to 9 users a 50% discount, compared to the standard USDT taker fee rate; the table lists 0.0400% taker for a regular user, 0.0150% for VIP 4 and 0.0085% for VIP 9. Binance's fee page repeats that all regular and VIP 1 to 9 users get 0 maker fee and up to 50% discounts on taker fees when trading any U (United Stable)- Margined Perps during the Promotion Period. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-02)

Bitfinex's announcement of Wednesday, December 17, 2025 says fees for all maker and taker activity on Bitfinex platforms will no longer be charged, effective immediately, with zero fees applying to products including derivatives trading. Its fee schedule lists derivatives trades with maker fees Zero and taker fees Zero. The Zero Fees Q&A says this is not a short term promotion, that there is no fixed end date, and that zero maker and taker fees apply to all trading pairs within the eligible product categories. Forbes says the announcement positions this as a long-term strategy rather than promotional activity, and Coinspeaker (via Yahoo Finance) says the change has no defined date to end. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Check the fee your API orders actually pay before sizing a strategy on a zero-fee headline. MEXC's own API comparison tells readers to check each venue's API fee schedule before deploying, because it can differ from the fee page; KCEX's blog says a trader who builds a bot using a promotional web fee may discover that the API has a separate schedule; Bitfinex's summary endpoint documents DERIV_TAKER_FEE and DERIV_REBATE; and Binance's change log lists the GET /fapi/v1/commissionRate endpoint to get user commission rate. (high confidence)

MEXC's own 0-Fee Fest page states that institutional accounts, market makers, project teams and API users are not eligible for 0 fees. The MEXC 'best zero-fee exchanges' article repeats that MEXC's event terms exclude API users, institutions and market makers from zero-fee promotions. The headline zero-fee futures rate therefore does not describe an API strategy on MEXC. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-19)

BingX announced zero trading fees on TradFi perpetual futures for eligible users in certain regions starting 2026-11-19 (UTC+8). The announcement says the zero-fee promotion applies exclusively to TradFi Perpetual Futures, and that other futures trading, spot trading, and API trading are excluded. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

MEXC's 0-Fee Fest notices exclude API traders. The notice adding NVDAUSDT, SOXLUSDT, SOXLUSDC and SOXLUSD1 to the 0-Fee Fest says 'Zero fees do not apply to API trading' and that zero fees do not apply to liquidation. The 0-Fee Fest page also says institutional accounts, market makers, project teams, and API users are not eligible for 0 fees. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

MEXC announced it would enable API access for selected BTC and ETH Spot trading pairs starting on Mar 1, 2026, 08:00 (UTC), and its futures API launched on Mar 31, 2026, 06:00 (UTC). Earlier, MEXC announced it would temporarily disable API for all trading pairs for upgrade and maintenance on July 25, 2022 2:30 (UTC), after which users would not be able to place orders for any futures trading pairs through the API. A ccxt commenter wrote on Nov 30, 2023 that under api permissions it says trading under maintenance. A freqtrade commenter wrote on Jan 10, 2025 that big pairs are not available via API for customers. (medium confidence)

MEXC will gradually migrate its Futures WebSocket market data feeds from JSON to Protocol Buffers (Protobuf). Clients that still receive Futures market data through WebSocket feeds in JSON format must update and test their API integrations to support Protobuf before the migration deadline of Dec 1, 2026, 10:00 (UTC). MEXC's API Updates feed also says MEXC would officially enable a new access domain for Futures APIs on Jan 12, 2026, 10:00 (UTC). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-12)

MEXC's futures API guide says its Open-API directly supports three request sources: APP, WEB, and OPEN-API. For WEB or APP requests the Authorization header carries the corresponding token value, while OPEN-API requests use ApiKey, Request-Time, Signature and optional Recv-Window headers. Public repos use the browser WEB-token route: hostnes/MexcApiBypass requires a 'WEB' format access token obtained from a browser session; vecful/mexc-futures-api sells a Futures API SDK for $120 and advertises trading even during official API maintenance; oboshto/mexc-futures-sdk warns that it uses browser session tokens and reverse-engineered endpoints and that MEXC does not officially support futures trading through API. MEXC's launch notice reserves the right to suspend or revoke API access in cases of abuse. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

BingX has run several TradFi zero-fee windows. A pilot ran from 2026-02-11 12:00 (UTC+8) to 2026-03-13 12:00 (UTC+8) in select regions; its rules say accounts that have created an API Key are not eligible for the zero-fee policy (regardless of whether API trading is used) and that users should delete the API Key first to participate. A BingX blog describes a zero-fee campaign for BingX TradFi Futures running from April 13 to July 31, with partners and affiliates continuing to receive full commissions through platform-funded subsidies. The promotion starting 2026-11-19 (UTC+8) gives zero trading fees on TradFi perpetual futures to eligible users in certain regions, applies exclusively to TradFi Perpetual Futures with other futures trading, spot trading, and API trading excluded, and has an end date to be announced separately. BingX reserves the right to revoke eligibility and recover related fee reductions if wash trading, arbitrage, or other violations are detected. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

Per Deribit's insights post, its fee schedule changed effective from the 1st of August 2026. Deribit's fee page lists Standard perpetuals and futures fees of 1.5 / 3.5 bps (maker/taker) with no criteria; VIP1 at 0 / 3 bps with criteria of $100k USDC equity, or $250k total equity; and VIP4 to VIP7 at -0.2 / 1.75, -0.3 / 1.5, -0.4 / 1.4 and -0.4 / 1.4 (negative maker fees represent maker rebates). A later post says new, lower taker fees for VIP4 through VIP7 take effect on 19 October 2026: 1.75, 1.50, 1.40 and 1.40 bps. Deribit's fee page lists API usage among the additional things it does not charge fees for. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Confirm the fee a given API key pays from account data, not from the banner. Deribit's fee page says you can view your fee discount level using private/get_account_summary or private/get_account_summaries methods (with the extended:true parameter). Bitfinex's Q&A says to review trade history or check the Fee Schedule to confirm that maker and taker fees for the relevant products are set to zero. The oboshto MEXC SDK README says getOrderHistory returns the takerFeeRate / makerFeeRate actually applied to each filled order. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bybit's TradFi FAQ says Zero-Fee mode includes commission costs directly in the spread for simpler pricing, while Tight-Spread mode offers narrower spreads with commissions calculated and applied separately. Bybit TradFi connects users to forex, commodities, indices and stock CFDs. That makes Zero-Fee mode a spread-priced product, not a zero-fee perpetual. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Bitfinex's authenticated API handles derivative orders. The WebSocket New Order doc says it creates a new order and can be used to create margin, exchange, and derivative orders, and documents an optional lev field (between 1 and 100 inclusive, default leverage value of 10) for derivative symbol orders only. The REST Submit Order doc says you may sum flag values to pass multiple flags, for example 4160 (64 + 4096) means Hidden and Post Only; it has a ROUTING field indicating origin of action, BFX or API>BFX; and a protect_selfmatch flag can be used to avoid matching orders with standing orders on the same account. (medium confidence)

AlphaX advertises no maker or taker trading commission across every available Spot, Crypto Futures, and TradFi pair for eligible users in supported regions. Its FAQ says fees may be adjusted in the future as the platform grows, with advance notice before any changes, and that funding rates, spreads, withdrawal fees and other service fees may still apply. A Cryptopolitan press release dated November 20, 2026 says the zero-fee initiative attracted more than 250,000 new registered users globally in the third quarter of 2026 and that AlphaX surpassed $1 billion in daily trading volume in Q3 2026; an Incrypted article says AlphaX said it attracted more than 250,000 newly registered users in a single quarter. These figures come from the company, not an independent audit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-22)

Binance's TradFi perpetuals notices say Binance reserves the right to disqualify participants who tamper with Binance program code, or interfere with the operation of Binance program code with other software, and participants showing signs of fraudulent behavior, such as wash trading, bulk account registrations, self dealing, and market manipulation. They also say Qualified Market Makers in the USDⓈ-M Futures Liquidity Provider Program will follow their weekly maker rebate tiers as usual for TradFi Perps, and that the taker discount in the USDⓢ-M Futures Taker Program will also apply to TradFi Perps. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04)

Binance's USDⓈ-M API change log shows POST /fapi/v1/stock/contract, added in the 2025-12-11 entry together with GET /fapi/v1/tradingSchedule and a tradingSession WebSocket method, to sign the TradFi-Perps agreement contract; POST /papi/v1/um/stock/contract, added in the 2026-04-08 Portfolio Margin entry, to sign the TradFi-Perps agreement contract; and, effective on 2025-11-26, RPI commisson fee is available in the response of the User Commission Rate endpoint GET /fapi/v1/commissionRate, which the change log describes as an endpoint to get user commission rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

BingX announced on 2026-11-17 02:48 zero trading fees on TradFi perpetual futures for eligible users in certain regions starting 2026-11-19 (UTC+8), with the end date to be announced separately. The announcement says 'Other futures trading, spot trading, and API trading are excluded', and that if wash trading, arbitrage, or other violations are detected, BingX reserves the right to revoke eligibility and recover related fee reductions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-17)

Binance's 2026-11-04 notice says that change will not be implemented, the 50% discount continues, and the promotion has run since 2026-03-31. Summaries built on the mirror are out of date.
